question: During the late 17th century, the English factory at Surat was involved in a conflict known as 'Child's War' (1686-1690). What was the primary cause of this conflict, and how did it conclude?
options: Sir John Child attempted to annex Surat; the Mughals expelled the English from Western India permanently
Sir John Child seized Mughal pilgrim ships to Mecca to enforce trade demands; Emperor Aurangzeb retaliated by besieging Bombay and forcing the EIC to pay a heavy fine and apologize
The English refused to pay transit duties; the local governor of Surat arrested all English factors until King William III intervened diplomatically
A rivalry between the Old and New English Companies led to the blockade of Surat port, resolved by the union of both companies in 1708
explanation: Sir John Child, Governor of Bombay, attempted to blockade Mughal ports and seize pilgrim ships going to Mecca to force Aurangzeb to grant more concessions. In response, Aurangzeb launched a massive offensive, captured the English factory at Surat, besieged Bombay, and only pardoned the English in 1690 after they paid a massive fine of 150,000 rupees and promised to behave.
